# Ginux: Building an Independent Kernel That Runs Linux Userspace through Human-Directed Agentic Engineering

### Authors/Creators

- Kurtzer, Gregory 1

- 1. CIQ

## Description

This report presents Human-Directed Agentic Engineering (HDAE), a method for building complex software by combining human-defined architecture, constraints, milestones, acceptance criteria, and stopping points with an autonomous implementation, execution, diagnosis, and revision loop. The experiment examines what this development model can accomplish and the domain expertise and executable validation required to keep it aligned

Ginux serves as the experimental case study. Over eleven days, one persistent coding-agent task produced an independent Rust-first x86-64 kernel that boots through UEFI, implements its own core operating-system mechanisms and Linux compatibility layer, executes selected unmodified Alpine Linux programs, and boots a Rocky Linux 10 userspace with systemd through multi-user.target.

Ginux demonstrates the rapid integration of established systems mechanisms, but it remains a research prototype. Its compatibility and hardware coverage are narrow, it has not received an independent security audit, and it makes no claim to production readiness or equivalence with Linux.

### Authors/Creators

- Anonymous, Anonymous

## Description

This deposit contains a pseudonymised export of a single, unplanned conversation between a user and DeepSeek's chat model, conducted over six days (19–25 October 2026). It began as a request to analyse a personal essay on forgiveness written about twenty years earlier and grew, without a prior plan, into an extended exchange covering psychological meta-analysis, a cumulative list of 143 analytical labels the model called "domains," family-history research, and a comparison of two short texts written in 2012 and 2026.

The conversation tree holds 1,788 message nodes. The final branch contains 742 user turns and 746 model turns, about 559,000 words, 52 model-initiated web searches, and 15 image uploads; a further 296 nodes sit on edited or regenerated branches and are preserved in the JSON. User turns are short (median 8 words); the model produced roughly 97 percent of the text.

## Technical info

This archive documents a sustained, self-directed intellectual investigation in which I used artificial intelligence as an external analytical environment. Through recursive questioning, historical comparisons, interdisciplinary integration, and repeated critical evaluation of the AI model’s conclusions, the interaction evolved from personal reflection into an extensive exploration of human cognition, knowledge organization, and artificial intelligence reasoning.

The resulting conversation demonstrates a process of human-directed inquiry and AI-generated conceptual synthesis, highlighting both the potential of extended human–AI collaboration and the limitations of AI-generated analysis, particularly regarding factual accuracy, scientific validation, and evidentiary reliability.

Data Privacy and Redaction Notice: This archive has been redacted to remove personal and identifying information. Consequently, certain details, references, and contextual elements are omitted. However, the majority of the original conversation, including its analytical progression, central discussions, and overall structure, has been preserved to support independent examination and further research.
